Definition: from G18 and G4160; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous:--them that do well.
BiblicalUsage: Agathopoios is a well-doer — a person whose life is marked by doing good — and it appears once, in Peter's teaching on government: rulers are sent 'for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well.' The word names the citizen whose life is so plainly good that even the authorities have to praise it. One word, one verse, and a whole ethic of quiet, visible goodness.
TheologicalSignificance: I treat this as vocabulary, not doctrine: useful for reading the verse rightly, but not a truth to build on by itself; in this case, the verse is 1 Peter 2:14.
